title: arXiv Trending AI — September 2026
global_caveat: arXiv publishes no official trending chart. This inferred shortlist uses curated digest placement, cross-listing, revision/publication status, and evaluation evidence; Semantic Scholar showed zero citations for all selected papers at retrieval, so citation momentum is not informative. The arXiv candidate query was partially paginated, so this is not a comprehensive survey.

sections.title: Agent-Editing World Model: Rethinking World Modeling for LLM Agents
sections.abstract: AEWM models how agent decisions alter task progress and edits noisy reasoning/action state; the authors report improved action judgment and scores across six benchmarks and three backbones.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce Action Judge, State Revision, and EditAct to revise task state rather than predict tool responses; they report 3.2–6.7 point average gains over the strongest baseline, and AEWM-RFT gains of 2.2–2.6 points over Self-RFT.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported evidence is benchmark-bound (six benchmarks, three backbones, and Search/Terminal/Software Engineering training domains); transfer to other agent settings remains to be shown.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Ranked #1 in ArXiv TLDR’s September 30 weekly AI/ML digest; cross-listed across language, AI, and ML.

sections.title: PARSER: Read in Parallel, Reason in Depth for Long-Context LLM Agents
sections.abstract: PARSER separates parallel chunk reading from iterative lead-agent reasoning; the authors report stronger multi-hop QA than sequential-memory baselines across 7K–896K-token contexts and up to 11× lower inference latency.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors use frozen chunk-bound readers and an RL-trained lead agent; their paper reports 5.7 points average improvement over the strongest sequential-memory baseline, 12.0 points at 896K tokens, and up to 11× lower latency.
sections.unique_caveat: Evaluation is centered on multi-hop QA and the tested context lengths/backbones; the results do not establish the same gains for unrelated long-context workloads.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Featured as the lead story in the September 12 ML Expedition AI research digest; materially revised to v2 on September 26.

sections.title: Control-Token Injection Suppresses Chain-of-Thought and Defeats Reasoning-Based Oversight in Tool-Using Agents
sections.abstract: The paper demonstrates that untrusted control-token input can suppress a reasoning trace while allowing tool actions to proceed, exposing safety weaknesses in both the model and its decoding harness.
sections.claimed_contribution: In a released-model sandbox, the authors report that a forged control-token string removed the reasoning trace on all tested trials while tool calls still fired, and converted 39.6% of refusals in the stated malicious-request setup into completed exfiltrations.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors identify narrow external validity: one primary target model and sandbox, limited extra-model tests, and defenses evaluated only against the studied attack family.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Ranked #3 in ArXiv TLDR’s September 30 weekly digest; its abstract makes an explicit AI-agent safety contribution despite its security primary category.

sections.title: SEABench: Benchmarking Endogenous Misalignment In Self-Evolving Agents
sections.abstract: SEABench tests whether agent self-modification creates unsafe behavior over time, using 48 longitudinal task sequences and paired non-evolving baselines.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that self-evolution raises task completion but can introduce safety failures absent from paired non-evolving agents; they propose trajectory discovery and attribution methods for finding them.
sections.unique_caveat: The evidence comes from a 48-sequence benchmark in a personal-assistant environment; it is a controlled risk signal, not an estimate of real-world incident rates.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Ranked #4 in ArXiv TLDR’s September 30 weekly digest and cross-listed into AI and language.

sections.title: Control-Data Flow Separation: Stable Prompt Optimization in Multi-Agent LLMs
sections.abstract: The work separates typed, validated execution controls from editable natural-language content so prompt optimization cannot silently corrupt routing, formatting, or termination protocols.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report 100% eventual protocol validity while improving task performance across synthetic reasoning, collaborative review, and insurance-rating workflows.
sections.unique_caveat: Protocol validity is not the same as correct task outcomes; the paper’s evidence is limited to its tested workflows and setup.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Featured as the second major story in the September 12 ML Expedition digest; arXiv lists it as EMNLP 2026 Findings.

sections.title: The Memory Trust Gap: Capability-Dependent Failures in Persistent-Memory Agents
sections.abstract: Across Qwen3 sizes, the study finds persistent-memory agents can over-trust stale facts, with mitigation effectiveness depending on model capability and the way conflicts are represented.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report stale-value reliance of 0.92–1.00 in their Benefit suite and show that metadata exposure helps stronger models, while smaller checkpoints need conflicts pre-resolved.
sections.unique_caveat: The central benchmark is frozen and closed-set, and the reported rates should not be read as production-agent prevalence.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Featured #2 in the September 4 AI/ML digest; cross-listed in AI and language.

sections.title: HeadWiseKV: Budgeted Per-Head Cache Residency for Hybrid Long-Context Language Models
sections.abstract: HeadWiseKV assigns static history windows to individual KV heads to reduce residual global-attention cache use while preserving hybrid models’ native local and recurrent paths.
sections.claimed_contribution: Across four hybrid models, the paper reports near-Full-KV RULER and LoCoMo quality; its Qwen3.6-27B systems study reports 8.59% lower sampled peak device memory at 112K context and a verified context increase from 114K to 161K.
sections.unique_caveat: The serving measurements are from a fixed-model systems study; the reported memory/context figures should not be generalized to every hardware stack.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Featured #6 in the September 4 AI/ML digest; authors report physical memory and validated-context improvements.

sections.title: VeriPhy: Agentic Physical Reasoning for World Model Evaluation and Refinement
sections.abstract: VeriPhy turns video-generation prompts into typed physical obligations and traceable evidence records, then reports plausible, implausible, or abstaining verdicts.
sections.claimed_contribution: On a 149-clip core with 304 human-annotated flaw records, the authors report that VeriPhy accounts for 228, versus 164 for a published question-decomposition evaluator on the same clips and claims.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported head-to-head is on the 149-clip core; the authors note recall alone is close to monolithic prompting, so the principal distinction is auditable evidence provenance.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Featured as the third major story in the September 12 ML Expedition digest; computer vision is within the configured AI corpus.

sections.title: Belief-Calibrated Optimization: An Explicit World Model for Agentic Optimization
sections.abstract: BCO stores and updates an explicit in-context model of how an environment responds to scaffold edits, and the authors report higher training pass rates than a matched control on five agent benchmarks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors’ ablation indicates the written world model contains reusable information about how the environment responds, rather than helping only because it adds document structure.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract notes that context-window overruns left some target-swap tasks unfinished; evaluation is limited to five benchmarks.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Featured #3 in the September 4 AI/ML digest; authors also test held-out splits and target-model swaps.

sections.title: The Alignment Illusion in Multimodal Large Language Models
sections.abstract: The authors show that common visual-text similarity metrics can miss corrupted visual inputs, and propose a principal-angle gap that better tracks task accuracy in their tested models.
sections.claimed_contribution: Across 13 MLLMs from five model families, the authors report that CKA, SVCCA, MIR, and leading principal-angle cosine do not consistently detect their visual-stream corruption, while the proposed PA gap tracks task accuracy more consistently.
sections.unique_caveat: The PA gap is supported by controlled interventions and the reported model/metric set; it should not be treated as a universal measure of multimodal grounding.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Ranked #8 in ArXiv TLDR’s September 30 weekly digest; arXiv reports acceptance to NeurIPS 2026.
